intended_object: The energy (index) of a vertex partition P = {V_1,…,V_k} with respect to a graph G: the normalized sum of squared edge densities d(V_i,V_j)^2 over pairs of distinct parts. It is the potential function driving the refinement step in Szemerédi's regularity lemma. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body computes (Σ over ordered pairs of distinct parts (U,W) of edgeDensity(U,W)^2) / k^2, where k = #P.parts. The proof applies this to equipartitions. There the textbook weights |U||W|/n^2 are essentially 1/k^2, so this is the standard index. It equals (2/k^2)·Σ_{i<j} d^2; Komlós–Simonovits use 1/k^2 before the sum over i<j, so the two differ by a factor of 2, which is a matter of normalization. The value lies in [0,1]. The definition already holds for an arbitrary Finpartition of a Finset in any type with decidable equality and any SimpleGraph with decidable adjacency. Taking values in ℚ is natural because edge densities are rational, and coe_energy casts it into any ordered field. It matches the cited formalisation by Dillies–Mehta. Mathlib has no other, more general version.
